title: Information Architecture & Product Hierarchy — Audit / Design Definition Only

current_primary_navigation.consistency_issue: 4 of 5 items resolve to a real index/hub page; 'Tools' resolves directly to one specific tool (metric-to-imperial-screw-converter), not a /tools/ hub — no /tools/index.html exists anywhere in the repository.
current_primary_navigation.mobile_behavior: flex-wrap; no hamburger/toggle exists anywhere in CSS or JS; all 5 items remain visible and simply wrap to additional lines on narrow viewports

current_footer_navigation.notes: Standards and Data Methodology are present in the footer (added in D1.1) but not the header. Thread Atlas (the flagship Engineering Data Product) has no footer entry at all — only 'Data Methodology' is listed, not the Atlas itself.
current_footer_navigation.spanish_footer_parity_gap: es/ pages use a materially different, older footer: footer_nav_center is only ['Herramientas','Gráficos','Tamaños','Guías'] (missing Reference entirely), footer_nav_right is only ['Acerca de','Contacto','Privacidad'] (missing Cookie Notice/Terms/Disclaimer entirely). This is a known, previously-documented, intentional D1.1/D1.2 scoping decision (English-only methodology/legal pages), not a new defect, but it is a material EN/ES structural difference relevant to this audit.

homepage_hierarchy.primary_action_communicated: Use the converter tool (hero is a live calculator widget, first thing seen)
homepage_hierarchy.product_positioning_communicated: A converter/calculator utility with supporting guides and reference pages — not a platform

reference_hub_sections.title: Thread engineering
reference_hub_sections.issue: This section title is a mislabel: 3 of its 4 cards (Standards, Thread Atlas, Data Methodology) are not 'thread engineering' topics — they are the Standards Library and Engineering Data Products families plus the methodology page, grouped under a section name that already refers to something narrower (the Thread Engineering reference cluster, itself the 1st card).

hub_hierarchy.standards_hub_structure: reference/standards/index.html lists all 6 standards families (ISO, ASME, DIN, ANSI, JIS, British); ISO is fully developed, the other 5 are thin stubs (per D1.3 finding, ASME now partially enriched) — content-quality status unchanged from D1.3, not re-audited here
hub_hierarchy.data_products_structure: No dedicated 'Engineering Data Products' hub page exists. Thread Atlas and Metric Thread Atlas are siblings only by convention (both Dataset-schema pages under /reference/), not grouped under any common index page.

cross_family_connectivity.tools_to_reference: confirmed present in body content on sampled tool pages (thread-identifier.html, tap-drill-calculator.html link to reference/thread-engineering/, reference/thread-types, reference/screw-anatomy, etc.)
cross_family_connectivity.tools_to_standards: NOT present in body content on sampled tool pages — only reachable via the generic sitewide footer link to /reference/standards/, not a contextual recommendation
cross_family_connectivity.tools_to_data_products: NOT present in body content on sampled tool pages; no tool page links to /reference/thread-atlas or /reference/metric-thread-atlas
cross_family_connectivity.reference_to_tools_standards_data: confirmed strong — reference/standards/iso.html and reference/thread-engineering/index.html both have explicit 'Related tools', 'Related charts' sections
cross_family_connectivity.standards_to_reference_data: confirmed strong on iso.html (full cross-link sections); the 4 remaining thin stub pages have no cross-links (D1.3 finding, unchanged)
cross_family_connectivity.related_content_blocks_assessment: Per D1.3's discovery and duplication audits, 'Related on BoltLab' / 'Related tools' / 'Related charts' blocks are consistently present on well-developed pages, use reasonable link density, and do not overemphasize any one family — they mitigate but do not replace the primary-navigation gap for Standards/Data Products

user_journey_assessment.tool_to_data_forward_journey: Partially supported: Tool → Reference is well-linked; Reference → Standards → Data Products is well-linked (within the Reference hub); but Tool → Standards/Data Products has no direct link, forcing a detour through Reference first.
user_journey_assessment.reference_reverse_journey: Supported: Reference pages link back to Tools and forward to Standards/Data via 'Related' sections.
user_journey_assessment.standards_reverse_journey: Supported on iso.html only; the 4 thin stub pages (unchanged from D1.3) have no outbound links to Reference, Data, or Tools beyond one link back to the Standards hub.

mobile_assessment.nav_behavior: CSS flex-wrap; all 5 header items remain visible on all viewport sizes, just wrap onto additional lines
mobile_assessment.conclusion: Mobile does not hide or further de-prioritize any navigation item beyond what already exists on desktop — the Standards/Data Products absence from the header is identical on mobile and desktop, not a mobile-specific regression

language_parity_assessment.header_parity: Spanish header nav mirrors English exactly in structure (5 items, same hrefs except homepage), including a 'Referencia' link to the English-only /reference/ hub
language_parity_assessment.footer_parity: Material gap — Spanish footer_nav_center omits 'Reference' entirely (only Tools/Charts/Sizes/Guides) and footer_nav_right omits Cookie Notice/Terms/Disclaimer (only About/Contact/Privacy)
language_parity_assessment.root_cause: documented, intentional scoping decision from D1.1/D1.2 (methodology and legal pages are English-only) — not a new discovery, flagged here as a structural IA difference for planning purposes only

findings.summary: Primary header navigation contains no item representing Standards Library or Engineering Data Products — 2 of BoltLab's 4 declared primary product families are absent from the one navigation element present on every page.
findings.evidence: index.html header nav-list: Tools, Charts, Reference, Sizes, Guides only. Confirmed identical on all 223 pages (site-wide header convention) and on Spanish pages.

findings.summary: The homepage never mentions or links Standards or Engineering Data Products anywhere in its visible body content (6 sections, 0 occurrences); its hero H1 frames BoltLab as a single converter tool, not a platform.
findings.evidence: grep for 'standards'/'atlas'/'data-methodology'/'engineering data' in index.html returns only the 2 footer-link occurrences; H1 is 'Universal Screw & Bolt Converter'.

findings.summary: No dedicated Tools hub page exists; the header's 'Tools' item deep-links directly to one specific tool rather than an index of all 8 tools, unlike its sibling nav items which all resolve to real hub pages.
findings.evidence: No tools/index.html in repository; header href is /tools/metric-to-imperial-screw-converter.

findings.summary: The Reference hub groups Standards Library, Engineering Data Products (Thread Atlas), and Data Methodology under a section literally titled 'Thread engineering' — a label that already refers to a narrower, different concept (the Thread Engineering reference cluster) also present in the same section.
findings.evidence: reference/index.html section 2 heading is 'Thread engineering' and contains cards for Thread Engineering Reference, Engineering standards hub, Unified Thread Atlas, and Engineering Data Methodology.

findings.summary: The footer lists 'Data Methodology' but has no direct entry for the Thread Atlas (the actual flagship Engineering Data Product) — it is one click further away than Standards or Data Methodology.
findings.evidence: footer-nav-center items: Tools, Charts, Reference, Standards, Data Methodology, Sizes, Guides — no 'Thread Atlas' or 'Data Products' entry.

findings.summary: Charts' claim to top-level header status is weaker than Tools/Reference/Sizes/Guides — it functions largely as an alternate presentation of data already covered by Reference and Sizes, rather than a distinct product family with unique intent.
findings.evidence: 9 chart pages; content overlaps thread/size data already covered in reference/ and sizes/ (cross-referenced in D1.3's page inventory).

findings.summary: EN/ES footer structural parity gap — Spanish footer omits Reference, Standards, Data Methodology, and all D1.2 legal links, unlike the English footer.
findings.evidence: es/index.html footer-nav-center = [Herramientas, Gráficos, Tamaños, Guías]; footer-nav-right = [Acerca de, Contacto, Privacidad]. Documented, intentional D1.1/D1.2 scoping decision, not new.

findings.summary: Sizes (115 pages) and Guides (13 pages) top-level nav placement is appropriate given their scale and D1.3-confirmed distinct search intent per sub-cluster.
findings.evidence: D1.3 duplication audit found 0 duplicative pages in the sizes/ cluster; each suffix serves a genuinely different query intent.

findings.summary: Related-content blocks ('Related tools', 'Related charts', 'Related on BoltLab') function well: reasonable link density, no overemphasis of any one family, genuine workflow value.
findings.evidence: D1.3 discovery and duplication audits; re-confirmed by spot-checking tool→reference cross-links in this phase.

findings.summary: Mobile navigation is not a separate problem — it inherits IA-P1-1 identically from desktop, with no additional mobile-specific hiding or de-prioritization.
findings.evidence: No hamburger/toggle exists; nav-list uses flex-wrap, all items remain visible at all viewport widths.

recommended_information_architecture.special_review_answer: C + D (combined): Standards and Engineering Data Products should receive meaningfully stronger primary discovery than they currently have (buried in footer text and one sub-section of the Reference hub) — but this does not require the literal four-family model (Tools/Reference/Standards/Data Products) to replace the current five-item header wholesale. Sizes and Guides have earned their place through scale and confirmed distinct intent (D1.3); Charts has a weaker but not clearly disqualifying claim. The four-family model should remain the conceptual/editorial organizing spine (as already established via the Data Methodology page), while the *visible* navigation is treated as a separate, evidence-based decision for D1.5 to make — not dictated by this audit.

rejected_options.A_current_five_item_nav_is_correct: Rejected as-is — the complete absence of Standards/Data Products from the header, combined with their complete absence from the homepage body, is a real gap given they are declared primary product families.
rejected_options.B_demote_current_items_to_subcategories: Not evidenced — Sizes and Guides have proven distinct value at their current scale; no finding in this audit or D1.3 supports demoting them.
rejected_options.E_wholesale_different_hierarchy: Not evidenced — no finding suggests the current five-item structure is fundamentally broken, only incomplete with respect to 2 families.

candidate_directions_for_d1_5_to_evaluat: Direction 1 — Minimal: add Standards and/or a combined 'Standards & Data' entry to the header (6th item), leaving Charts/Sizes/Guides untouched.

Direction 2 — Consolidation: relabel 'Reference' in the header to something that signals it contains Standards/Data (e.g., a label change or a mega-menu/dropdown revealing Reference/Standards/Data as siblings on hover) without adding a 6th top-level slot.

Direction 3 — Homepage-only fix: leave header untouched, but add a Standards/Data Products presence to the homepage body (a new section or card row) so first-time visitors see the platform's full scope without waiting to reach the Reference hub.

Direction 4 — Reference hub relabel: rename the 'Thread engineering' section on the Reference hub to something that doesn't collide with the Thread Engineering cluster's own name (e.g., splitting it into two clearly-labeled sections).
recommended_information_architecture.note: This audit does not select among these directions. That selection, and any navigation/label/link change, belongs to a subsequent implementation-authorized phase.
